prs.title: Editorial: remove incorrect note about [[NoTear]]
prs.author: michaelficarra
prs.body: A Shared Data Block event's `[[NoTear]]` field is typically (but not always) determined by `IsNoTearConfiguration`. This operation returns false for `Uint8ClampedArray`s and *sometimes* for `BigInt64Array`/`BigUint64Array`, depending on order. So this note is just disconnected from reality and should be removed.

prs.title: Editorial: Clarify parsing
prs.author: gibson042
prs.body:
In preparation for #3933, this PR splits a new Parsing section from The Syntactic Grammar and references both from ParseText.

It also performs some related cleanup, including consistent phrasing, a new Grammar Notation example, generalization of The Numeric String Grammar into Runtime Grammars, and generalization of \<ABBREV> to all non-syntactic grammars.

prs.title: Normative: make DataView.prototype.{byteLength,byteOffset} not throw when backed by detached buffer
prs.author: bakkot
prs.body:
Fixes https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/issues/2635. This makes these getters on DataViews behave like the corresponding getters on TypedArrays.

Note that these getters will still throw when `.call`'d on incompatible receivers; this is just about what happens when a real DataView's `.byteLength` or `.byteOffset` is invoked after the buffer backing said view has been detached or [become out of bounds](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/ArrayBuffer/resize).

This came up in the context of Web IDL, which has badly needed to rationalize its TypedArray handling for a long time; @MattiasBuelens has been working on that in https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/pull/1529 but encountered this inconsistency, which was surprising and also complicates that side of things (since webIDL normally treats DataViews and TypedArrays very similarly).

prs.title: Layering: Narrow [[ArrayBufferDetachKey]] to ECMAScript language value
prs.author: linusg
prs.body:
As suggested by @gibson042 in https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/pull/3976#discussion_r4049247770. The slot itself is currently not explicitly typed (that will be done in the aforementioned PR), so the type is only implied by the `DetachArrayBuffer` AO parameter.

Web specs that make use of this slot:

- https://webassembly.github.io/spec/js-api/#create-a-fixed-length-memory-buffer

  > Set buffer.[[ArrayBufferDetachKey]] to "WebAssembly.Memory".

- https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/#dom-gpubuffer-getmappedrange

  > Set view.[[ArrayBufferDetachKey]] to "WebGPUBufferMapping".

- https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#can-transfer-array-buffer

  > If SameValue(O.[[ArrayBufferDetachKey]], undefined) is false, return false.

- https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#buffersource-transferable

  > If jsArrayBuffer.[[ArrayBufferDetachKey]] is not undefined, then return false.

Inspecting several implementations confirm that ES language value is sufficiently broad to match real world usage, which is sometimes limited to the presence of a boolean flag rather than full value identity:

| Engine | Source | Type |
| - | - | - |
| Boa | core/engine/src/builtins/array_buffer/mod.rs#L210-L211 | `JsValue` |
| JavaScriptCore | Source/JavaScriptCore/runtime/ArrayBuffer.cpp#L517-L523 | N/A |
| Kiesel | https://codeberg.org/kiesel-js/kiesel/src/commit/25fea73ae80d942c12df6a9b90e5fea8e4088986/src/builtins/array_buffer.zig#L1073-L1074 | `Value` |
| LibJS | Userland/Libraries/LibJS/Runtime/ArrayBuffer.h#L145 | `Value
